title: reel asciicast annotation
description: The data of a reel annotation: an asciicast event with code "R", whose data is a JSON string holding this object. Other asciicast readers ignore the event. The object names its kind, and holds the fields of that kind. Kinds this schema does not list may hold any fields, so a reader keeps annotations written by newer tools.

kind.description: What the annotation records, as dot-separated lower case words, the first naming the tool that defines the kind, such as "reel.effect".

reel.effect.description: An effect of the profile an asciicast file was exported with, from reel's effects package, which reads it back to export the file again with the same effect. The "effect" field names the effect, and the other fields are its options, as the definition for that effect lists them. A field left out takes its default, and reel leaves out every field at its default. Durations are whole milliseconds. An effect never holds a secret: regions that match the values of environment variables hold their names only. reel writes one annotation for each effect, at offset 0, before the recording's events, in the order the effects run.

effect.description: The effect: "keys" overlays the keys pressed, "intro" shows a title card before the first frame, "pause" pauses playback with a pause badge, "highlight" draws attention to a region, "zoom" zooms in on one, "redact" hides a region from the frames, and "redact_inputs" hides typed text from the keys shown.

reel.effect.keys.description: The keys effect: an overlay of the keys pressed, in the bottom right corner of the terminal frames.

shown_ms.description: How long keys stay shown after the last key of a burst, fading out over its final third. Zero or less shows no keys.

reel.effect.intro.description: The intro effect: a card of lines of text shown before the first frame.

duration_ms.description: How long the card is shown, unscaled by the playback speed. Zero or less shows no card.

lines.description: The lines of the card, top to bottom, each centered. Left out, the card is the recording's title in bold, and a recording without a title gets no card.

reel.effect.line.description: A line of text on a card.

text.description: The text, drawn as it is: escape sequences are not interpreted.

reel.effect.style.description: How the text of a line is drawn. Left out, the text has the terminal's default colors and no attributes.

fg.description: The text color. Left out, the terminal's default.

bg.description: The background color. Left out, the terminal's default.

underline_color.description: The underline color. Left out, the text color.

underline.description: The underline's style. Left out, no underline.

attrs.description: The text attributes, in any order.

reel.effect.pause.description: The pause effect: pauses of playback on a frozen frame, at the end of the recording or at marks, each showing a pause badge, two bars on a translucent disc, in a corner of the terminal's cell grid.

points.description: Where playback pauses, and for how long. Left out, it pauses for 1000ms at the end. Pauses that fall on one step of a frame play as one, for the longest of them.

badge.description: Whether the pauses show the badge. Left out, true. Without the badge, the other badge fields are ignored.

badge_corner.description: The corner of the terminal's cell grid the badge is in. Left out, "top_right".

badge_size_px.description: The badge's diameter in pixels. Left out, or 0, one and a half times the height of a terminal cell, and at least 8.

badge_color.description: The color of the pause bars. Left out, "#eeeeee". The disc behind them is a translucent dark grey for a light color, and a translucent light grey for a dark one.

reel.effect.pause_point.description: Where a pause effect pauses, and for how long.

at.description: Where it pauses: "end" after the last terminal frame, "marks" at each mark with one of the labels, or at every mark without labels, and "match" at each mark whose label the pattern matches.

duration_ms.description: How long the pause lasts, unscaled by the playback speed. Zero is no pause.

labels.description: For "marks": the labels of the marks to pause at, each of which must name a mark in the recording. Left out, every mark.

pattern.description: For "match": a Go regular expression (RE2 syntax) matched against the labels of the marks.

reel.effect.highlight.description: The highlight effect: draws attention to the cells of a region by darkening the rest of the frame, and can draw an outline around them.

dim.description: How much everything outside the region is darkened, from 0, which leaves it alone, to 1, which makes it black. Left out, 0.5.

outline.description: A border drawn around each rectangle of cells the region covers, outside it and its padding. Left out, no outline.

color.description: The border's color. Left out, "#ffd75f", a warm yellow.

width_px.description: The border's width in pixels. Left out, or 0, an eighth of the height of a cell, and at least 1.

padding_px.description: The pixels around each rectangle of cells the region covers that are kept with it, undimmed, on every side. Left out, a third of the width of a cell, and at least 1.

reel.effect.zoom.description: The zoom effect: the terminal's cell grid shows the cells of a region larger.

scale.description: How many times larger the region is drawn than the terminal draws it. Left out, the region, with a cell of margin on every side, is fit to the grid, as large as it fits, and never smaller than the terminal draws it.

anchor.description: Where the region is placed in the grid: the point at fraction x, y of the region's width and height, from its top left, is drawn at the same fraction of the grid's. Left out, x and y are 0.5, which centers it.

x.description: The fraction of the width, from the left.

y.description: The fraction of the height, from the top.

reel.effect.redact.description: The redact effect: hides the cells of a region, such as a secret, from every frame, and the text of text, env, and regexp regions from the terminal's title and program status. reel never writes it, since an asciicast file holds what it hides, but reads it back.

timing.description: When the effect is on. Left out, for the whole recording. Unlike other effects, it cannot ease, since easing would show part of what it hides.

mode.description: How each cell is hidden: "block" as a blank cell in its background, "blur" as a blurred shape of text, and "replace" as the replacement character, in the cell's own colors. Left out, "block".

replacement.description: For the "replace" mode: the character each cell shows, a printable character one cell wide.

reel.effect.redact_inputs.description: The redact_inputs effect: hides the text a region matches from the typed text the keys effect shows, as a bullet for each character. Its region is a text, regexp, or env region, or any of them. reel never writes it, since an asciicast file holds what it hides, but reads it back.

reel.effect.min_partial.description: The fewest characters of the start or end of the text of a text or env region that are hidden where only that part of it shows, such as while it is typed. Text of this many characters or fewer is only hidden whole. Left out, 3.

reel.effect.timing.description: When an effect is on, and how it eases in and out. Left out, it is on for the whole recording, and switches on and off at once.

ease_in_ms.description: How long, in playback time, the effect eases in over before the start of its window. Left out, 0, which switches it on at once.

ease_out_ms.description: How long, in playback time, the effect eases out over after the end of its window. Left out, 0, which switches it off at once.

reel.effect.between.description: The window of the recording an effect is on in: from the first mark labeled from to the first mark labeled to after it. Each label must name a mark in the recording. Left out, the whole recording.

from.description: The label of the mark the window starts at. Left out, the start of the recording.

to.description: The label of the mark the window ends at. Left out, the end of the recording.

reel.effect.region.description: Cells of the terminal, matched on each frame: "cells" a rectangle of cells, "rows" whole rows, "text" the cells that show some text, "regexp" the cells a regular expression matches, "env" the cells that show the values of environment variables, and "any" the cells any of several regions covers. Text is matched line by line, where a line is a row and the rows it soft-wrapped over.

type.description: The type of region, which the definition for that type describes.

reel.effect.region.cells.description: The cells from column x0 and row y0 up to but not including column x1 and row y1, where 0, 0 is the top left cell. The part outside the screen is left out.

reel.effect.region.rows.description: Whole rows of the screen, counted from 0 at the top.

reel.effect.region.text.description: The cells that show some text, wherever and as often as it appears.

text.description: The text. Blank cells read as spaces. Empty text, and text with a line break, matches nothing.

reel.effect.region.regexp.description: The cells a regular expression matches, wherever and as often as it matches, against the text of each line on its own, so ^ and $ match at the ends of a line. A match covers every cell it holds any part of.

pattern.description: A Go regular expression (RE2 syntax), with leftmost-first matching.

reel.effect.region.env.description: The cells that show the values of environment variables, as they are where the recording is exported, matched as text, each line of a value on its own. A variable that is unset, or a value or line that is only whitespace, matches nothing.

names.description: The names of the variables. Only the names are stored, never the values.

reel.effect.region.any.description: The cells any of several regions covers.

reel.effect.color.description: A color: a palette index from 0 to 255, which the renderer maps through its palette, or a color in sRGB as "#rrggbb", or "#rrggbbaa" with an alpha that is not opaque.

reel.effect.rgb_color.description: A color in sRGB as "#rrggbb", or "#rrggbbaa" with an alpha that is not opaque, in hexadecimal digits.

reel.query.description: A query the program wrote to its terminal, such as for its device attributes or its background color, and the terminal's reply, which the program read as input. The file holds the replies nowhere else, since replaying the output makes the terminal reply again. reel writes one for each query, in the order the program wrote them, after the output event that held them, at its offset. A reply to a query reel did not find in that output, such as one split across two writes, is written after them, without a request. A session writes none when it is opened without queries.

query.description: What the program asked for: "enq" the answerback (ENQ), "da1", "da2", and "da3" the primary, secondary, and tertiary device attributes, "xtversion" the terminal's name and version, "dsr" a device status, "cpr" the cursor position, "color_scheme" whether the terminal is dark or light, "decrqm" a mode, "osc_color" a dynamic or palette color, "osc52" the clipboard, "kitty_keyboard" the kitty keyboard protocol flags, "decrqss" a setting, "xtgettcap" terminfo capabilities, "xtwinops" the window's size or state, "decrqcra" a checksum of a rectangle of cells, and "unknown" a reply to no query reel knows.

param.description: What the query asked about, where it names one: for "decrqm" the mode, with "?" before a DEC private mode, such as "?2026"; for "osc_color" the OSC number, such as "11" for the background, or "4" for the palette; for "osc52" the selection, such as "c"; for "decrqss" the setting, such as "m"; for "xtgettcap" the capability names, joined by ";"; for "xtwinops" the operation, such as "14"; and for "dsr" and "cpr" the status asked for, such as "5", "6", or "?6". Left out for other queries.

request.description: The query as the program wrote it, escape sequence and all. Left out for a reply whose query was not found.

reply.description: What the terminal answered, escape sequence and all, every reply in the order written when the query asked for more than one thing, such as two palette colors. Left out when the terminal did not answer.

truncated.description: True when the request or the reply was longer than 4 KiB, and cut to it. Left out otherwise.

steep.truncated.description: True when a text field of the annotation was longer than 4 KiB, and cut to it, on a character boundary. Left out otherwise.

steep.cell.description: A cell of the terminal's screen, counted from 0, 0 at the top left.

row.description: The row, from 0 at the top.

col.description: The column, from 0 at the left.

steep.match.description: Text found on the screen, as the test saw it: the text of each row, with ANSI sequences stripped when the harness strips them, rows joined by line breaks.

text.description: The text found. A match of a regular expression may span rows, joined by a line break.

row.description: The row the text starts on, from 0 at the top.

col.description: The column, in cells, the text starts at, from 0 at the left.

steep.dims.description: A width and a height, in cells, either of which is left out when it was not asserted.

steep.start.description: The start of a test run with steep, a test harness for Bubble Tea programs, with the harness's configuration, after any STEEP_ environment variables applied. steep writes it once, as the first event of the recording, before the program starts.

test.description: The name of the Go test, such as "TestLogin/bad_password".

cols.description: The terminal's width in cells as the program starts.

rows.description: The terminal's height in cells as the program starts.

timeout_ms.description: How long a wait may take before it fails the test.

check_ms.description: How often a wait checks the screen.

settle_ms.description: How long the screen, or the program's messages, must stay unchanged for a settle wait to be satisfied.

slow_ms.description: How long the harness sleeps after each action. Left out for none.

ansi.description: Whether assertions, waits, and snapshots compare the screen with its ANSI sequences kept. When false they are stripped first.

color.description: The color support the terminal advertises to the program. Left out when the test left it as it is, 256 colors.

export.description: When the harness exports its recording: "off" never, "failure" when the test fails, and "always".

messages.description: True when the harness records each message the program's model receives, as steep.message annotations. Left out otherwise.

steep.ready.description: The end of the harness's wait for the program to start, which ends when the program's model handles its first message. steep writes it once, after steep.start.

outcome.description: How the wait ended: "ready" when the program started, "timeout" when it did not start within the timeout, and "canceled" when the test's context was canceled first. The test goes on after a timeout or a cancelation.

elapsed_ms.description: How long the harness had run when the wait ended, in wall-clock time.

steep.input.description: Input the test sent the program through the terminal, before it was sent. The input event that follows holds the bytes the terminal sent, encoded in the program's keyboard and mouse modes, if it sent any: a mouse event the program has not enabled mouse tracking for sends nothing.

action.description: The input: "type" text typed as key presses, "key" a key press, "paste" a paste, "mouse" a mouse event, "click" a press and release of a mouse button, and "drag" a press of a mouse button, motion one cell at a time, and its release.

text.description: For "type" and "paste": the text. Left out when it is empty.

key.description: For "key": the key's name, with its modifiers, such as "enter" or "ctrl+c".

button.description: For "mouse", "click", and "drag": the mouse button, or "none" for motion without one.

at.description: For "mouse" and "click": the cell of the event. For "drag": the cell it starts at.

to.description: For "drag": the cell it ends at.

steep.terminal.description: A change the test made to the terminal that no other event records. Resizes, focus changes, and colors are their own events.

action.description: The change: "scrollback_size" set how many lines of history the terminal keeps, "clear_scrollback" cleared its history, and "clipboard" set the clipboard the terminal answers the program's clipboard reads with.

lines.description: For "scrollback_size": the lines of history kept.

text.description: For "clipboard": the clipboard's text. Left out when it is empty.

steep.program.description: An action of the test on the program past its terminal, which the program's output may show the effect of.

action.description: The action: "send" sent the program a message, "quit" asked it to quit, and "mutate" changed its model directly.

type.description: For "send": the message's Go type, such as "tea.KeyPressMsg". For "mutate": the Go type of the model changed.

value.description: For "send": the message's value, as Go's fmt package prints it with %+v.

steep.wait.start.description: The start of a wait of the test, for what the screen shows, for the program's messages, or for time to pass. The steep.wait.end with the same id ends it, unless the test ended first, such as by a panic.

id.description: The wait's number, counted from 1 for each test, which its steep.wait.end has too.

wait.description: What the test waits for: "text" every one of some text to be on the screen, "not_text" none of it to be, "match" a regular expression to match the screen, "not_match" it not to, "func" a condition of the test's own on the screen, "settle" the screen to stay unchanged for the settle time, "settle_messages" the program's model to receive no message for the settle time, "message" the program's model to receive a message of a type, "finished" the program to end, and "sleep" time to pass.

pattern.description: For "match" and "not_match": the regular expression, in Go's RE2 syntax. Left out when it is empty.

type.description: For "message": the Go type of message waited for, such as "tea.WindowSizeMsg", which may be an interface type.

live.description: For "message": true when only messages received after the wait starts count. Left out otherwise.

timeout_ms.description: How long the wait may take before it fails the test. Left out for "sleep".

settle_ms.description: For "settle" and "settle_messages": how long nothing must change.

duration_ms.description: For "sleep": how long it sleeps. Left out for no time.

steep.wait.end.description: The end of the wait the steep.wait.start with the same id started. A wait that is not satisfied fails the test, and a steep.failure with the reason comes before it.

id.description: The wait's number, as its steep.wait.start has it.

wait.description: What the test waited for, as its steep.wait.start has it.

outcome.description: How the wait ended: "satisfied" when what it waited for happened, "timeout" when it did not within the timeout, "canceled" when the test's context was canceled first, and "failed" for another failure, such as an invalid regular expression or a program that ended with an error.

elapsed_ms.description: How long the wait took, in wall-clock time.

matches.description: For a satisfied "text" wait: where each of the text first appears on the screen it was satisfied by. For a satisfied "match" wait: where the regular expression first matched it. Left out otherwise.

type.description: For a satisfied "message" wait: the Go type of the message that satisfied it.

steep.assert.description: An assertion of the test, on one sample of the screen or on the messages the program's model received, and whether it passed. One that fails fails the test, and a steep.failure with the reason comes before it. A required one that fails stops the test.

assert.description: What was asserted: "contains" every one of some text is on the screen, "not_contains" none of it is, "match" a regular expression matches the screen, "not_match" it does not, "width", "height", and "dimensions" the size of the screen's text, and "has_message" the program's model received a message of a type.

required.description: Whether a failure stops the test, as steep's Require methods do, rather than letting it go on, as its Assert methods do.

pattern.description: For "match" and "not_match": the regular expression, in Go's RE2 syntax. Left out when it is empty.

type.description: For "has_message": the Go type of message asserted, which may be an interface type.

actual.description: For "width", "height", and "dimensions": the size of the screen's text, both width and height.

matches.description: For a passing "contains": where each of the text first appears on the screen. For a passing "match": where the regular expression first matched it. Left out otherwise.

steep.snapshot.description: A comparison of the screen with a snapshot file, and whether it matched. One that does not match fails the test, and a steep.failure with the reason comes before it. A required one that does not match stops the test.

format.description: What was compared: "text" the screen's text, in a ".snap" file, and "json" the screen's cells and the terminal's state, in a ".json" file.

path.description: The snapshot file's path, as the test named it, relative to the test's package directory unless absolute.

required.description: Whether a mismatch stops the test.

pass.description: Whether the screen matched the file, or the file was written.

updated.description: True when the file was written with the screen instead of compared, as when snapshots are being updated. Left out otherwise.

missing.description: True when the file did not exist. Left out otherwise.

diff.description: For a "text" snapshot that did not match: a unified diff from the file to the screen.

steep.failure.description: A failure the harness reported to the test: a failed assertion, wait, or snapshot, an error of a harness action, or a timeout. Failures the test reports itself are not recorded.

message.description: The failure message, as the test's output shows it.

steep.message.description: A message the program's model received, before it handled it. steep writes these only when the test asks it to, since a program that ticks or animates receives many.

type.description: The message's Go type, such as "tea.KeyPressMsg".

value.description: The message's value, as Go's fmt package prints it with %+v.

steep.exit.description: The end of the program. A program that ends while the test runs, such as on a key that quits it, records it in the recording. One the harness stops at the end of the test records it after the recording ends, so the recording does not hold it.

error.description: The error the program ended with. Left out when it ended without one.

killed.description: True when the program was killed, as the harness kills a program that does not quit when asked. Left out otherwise.

steep.result.description: The test's result, as of the start of the harness's close, which ends the recording just after it. Failures after that, such as a program that does not stop, are not counted.

test.description: The name of the Go test.

failed.description: Whether the test had failed, or was panicking.

panicked.description: True when the test was panicking. Left out otherwise.

skipped.description: True when the test was skipped. Left out otherwise.

failures.description: How many failures the harness reported, each a steep.failure.

duration_ms.description: How long the harness had run, in wall-clock time.

stack.description: For a test that panicked: the stack of the goroutine that panicked, from the panic, as Go prints it.
